problem: Existing VLN agents align raw directional features and visual features (trained with one-hot labels) directly to instruction features. The large semantic gap between these modalities makes alignment hard and action decisions hard to interpret.
motivation: Instructions are composed of atomic actions (e.g. 'turn right') and object/scene concepts (e.g. 'kitchen'). Mapping observations into the same language space as concept phrases should bridge the modality gap, simplify alignment and make decisions interpretable, which matters for reliable real-world deployment.
key_idea: Map each single-view observation to a natural-language 'actional atomic concept' (an atomic action from the relative direction plus CLIP-predicted object concepts, re-ranked by the instruction) and use its embedding to regularize the observation features through contrastive co-embedding.
insight: Adding language-form concepts as a bridge improves alignment. In the R2R val-unseen ablation, SR rises from 66.67 (separate embedding) to 67.94 with concepts, and to 68.54 with the full model (concepts, contrastive regularization and refining adapter). Concepts that combine action and object beat either alone (SR 67.94 vs 66.37 object-only and 67.13 action-only). Top-k=5 objects is best, and the adapter re-ranks the ground-truth object higher (e.g. 'kitchen' moves from top-4 to top-1). Gains are larger on unseen splits, which suggests better generalization.
method: Object concept mapping: uses a frozen CLIP (ViT-B/32) to score each view image against 'a photo of a {object}' for objects in an in-domain repository built from training and augmentation instructions, and keeps the top-k=5 objects.

Atomic action concept mapping: computes the heading/elevation of each candidate relative to the previously selected action and maps it by rule (Table 1) to one of six actions: go up/down/forward/back, turn left/right. A 'stop' concept is added for the stop feature.

Concept refining adapter: a CLIP-Adapter-style two-layer MLP takes the image feature and the instruction [CLS] feature, with residual ratio alpha=0.8. It re-ranks the top-k object probabilities, and the concept feature is the probability-weighted sum of BERT-encoded 'action+object' phrases.

Observation co-embedding: keeps separate embeddings of view, direction and concept. An InfoNCE loss pulls the view+direction embedding toward its own concept embedding and away from the other views' concepts in the same panorama. The final observation feature is the sum of the visual and concept embeddings, and the same is applied to the history.
Training: plugged into HAMT and DUET, trained with A2C RL + λ1·IL + λ2·contrastive loss (λ1=0.2, λ2=1/1/0.01 for R2R/REVERIE/R2R-Last). The contrastive loss is not applied to history.

setting.backbone: HAMT and DUET (trained with AACL) + frozen CLIP ViT-B/32 image/text encoders, BERT-like concept encoder
setting.training_data: R2R, REVERIE and R2R-Last training sets (R2R also uses the augmentation data of VLN-BERT for the object repository); no extra data beyond the baselines' pipeline is stated
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views, CLIP/ViT features) with heading/elevation direction info

results: AACL improves both baselines on R2R, REVERIE and R2R-Last, especially on unseen splits. DUET+AACL reaches R2R val-unseen SR 74 (vs DUET 72) and REVERIE test-unseen SR 55.09 (vs DUET 52.51). HAMT+AACL improves R2R-Last val-unseen SR from 45.2 to 47.2.
limitations: Depends on a fixed CLIP and a repository of object words drawn from training instructions, so object concepts are limited to that vocabulary.
Action concepts come from a coarse rule-based set of six atomic actions and the previous heading, so they cannot express finer or more complex motions.
Some SPL/val-seen metrics do not improve (e.g. DUET SPL 73→72 on R2R val-seen, HAMT val-seen REVERIE SR drops), and gains on R2R are modest; there is no real-robot evaluation.
